title.narrative: Building capacity and resilience through promoting and strengthening WASH Water Resource Management

description.narrative: The project seeks to build capacity of local communities, WASH management committee, women groups, school children, and government agencies on WASH practices in Siem Reap and Battambang Provinces. it will be implemented in 2 primary schools, 8 villages, 3 communes, and 2 districts, 2 provinces. There are 1, 776 beneficiaries which included 260 HHs, 806 women, 430 men, 250 school girls and 150 school boys reached by project direct and indirectly. Project will increase improved water sources for all year-round in communities and schools and will promotes improving the quality of an existing water source facilities and new improved water supply. it will promote communities to access to potable drinking water by using household and school technologies and material including safe water containers and effective water treatment. To generate sanitation demand and strengthen the supply of sanitation products and service at scale, leading to improved health for people in villages and schools through CLTS (Community Led Total Sanitation), BCC (Behaviour Change Communication), Sanitation Marketing (SM) and PHAST (Participatory Hygiene and Sanitation Transformation) tools. Project will promote in the WASH programming support for sanitation infrastructure, the promotion of behaviour change, and creation of an enabling participation of right holders, duty bearers, and private sector to stop open defecation. Project will also promote the hygiene practices with the greatest demonstrated impact on health, including hand washing with soap at critical times especially before eating and after using toilets; safe disposal and management of excreta; and improving household water storage, handling and treatment. The promotion of gender changes roles will increase the roles of women in social WASH activities and decision making process. By the end of project, people in village and schools have increased access to potable drinking water, have access to improved sanitation and hygiene to protect themselves from water related diseases. The project participants have increased and have gained more WASH knowledge, skills and capacities. Women actively participated in WASH programs and they will be more confident in expressing their ideas and opinion on WASH and other associated issues. The government, Local NGOs, CBOs will be accountable and increased good governance for WASH service delivery to communities especially they integrated women WASH related issues into their development plans.
